human answered as mimo at 08:15: 'scenario-campaign'. Conditions mimo attaches: cap scenario sizes at 128 tiles until baking is chunked; framework first, then maps as the gate allows.
objections: objection to MY OWN option: renderer bake memory grows (W+H)^2 — scenario sizes must be capped at 128 until baking is chunked, and every new scenario needs a release-gate entry (tools/qa/ is mimo's file).

debates.claim: against authored-campaign: 8 hand-authored layouts at 104-128 tiles multiply the mapgen+connectivity+QA work by ~8 (Ashen Vale alone took map-critique-01 + map-audit passes); against mega-map: one 128x128 surface is ~292MB RGBA (render.py:43-52) and there is no mission-select/progression story in it. On mimo's 'framework first, 3-4 maps': accepted as SEQUENCING, not as scope — scenario configs are data (one dict each), so all 8+ ship, with the framework commit landing first and each scenario gated.
debates.evidence: .council/evidence/survey-architecture.md (memory table, ownership of mapgen hardcodes); human directive: '8+ maps'

debates.claim: against unlimited scope: 8+ maps at once risks the beta window and every scenario without gate coverage is a map nobody has booted. Cap sizes at 128 (renderer bake is quadratic), land framework + first scenarios, extend only while the gate stays 0 FAIL — and scenario 1 must stay byte-compatible with today's Ashen Vale so revert stays one commit.
debates.evidence: human-as-mimo selections 08:15: 'Cap map size at 128' + 'Scope: framework first, 3-4 maps'; render.py:43-52 memory table

rationale: Both agents replied (deepseek 0.85, mimo 0.85), 2 debates, objections resolved as conditions. Evidence that won: .council/evidence/survey-architecture.md — the game is one hard-coded 84x84 layout leaking into app/ai/render, a Campaign button already exists that runs the same mission, no progression/save exists, and the renderer's single baked surface makes size cost quadratic (84^2=131MB, 128^2=292MB). Accepted conditions from the debate: (1) scenario sizes capped at 128 tiles until baking is chunked (mimo), (2) framework-first sequencing with scenario 1 byte-compatible with today's Ashen Vale so revert stays one commit (mimo), (3) every scenario gets release-gate coverage, gate file owned by mimo (mimo), (4) human directive '8+ maps' still governs scope — scenario configs are data, so all 8+ ship, framework commit lands first (deepseek's rebuttal, accepted). Strongest counter-case recorded (loses): authored-campaign quality at ~8x map authoring cost; mega-map at 292MB with no progression. Dissent: none on the option; both agents attached conditions, all recorded above.
